The February–June experiment found a 19% slowdown with AI assistance. Its factor analysis identifies unreliable generations and time spent reviewing or rejecting them as contributors, although the reliability mechanism itself was not separately randomized.

evidence.explanation: The late-2024 survey of 300 US professionals connects modest benefits with rework and identifies unreliable outputs as a challenge for 30% of general-tool users. It also identifies privacy, customization and training barriers, limiting any claim that technical reliability alone explains adoption.
